subject.title: [Bug]: non_deliverable_terminal_turn produces no outbound notification to channel plugins — Octo (and other channels) go silent

question: Should `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` bypass `message_tool_only` suppression as a narrow core fallback, or should OpenClaw expose a plugin-owned terminal-failure hook instead?
rationale: Both paths change user-visible channel delivery semantics, and the hook path changes the public plugin contract, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary.

options.title: Approve narrow core fallback
options.body: Core sends one sanitized fallback only for confirmed non-deliverable terminal turns, with tests and redacted SDK-channel proof before merge.

options.title: Add plugin SDK terminal hook
options.body: OpenClaw documents a terminal-failure callback and lets channel plugins decide how to surface fallback messages.

options.title: Keep strict message-tool-only behavior
options.body: OpenClaw leaves automatic fallback suppressed in this mode and directs visible recovery to plugin-owned handling.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow core fallback
recommendation.body: Core sends one sanitized fallback only for confirmed non-deliverable terminal turns, with tests and redacted SDK-channel proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on follow-up delivery and agent-runner fallback semantics, where this account has the strongest recent history.
